What's different between all the brands of premium coolers?

There isn't much that separates the different premium cooler brands (Yeti, Orca, Pelican, Bison, Grizzly, K2, and Engel are the ones that readily come to mind). Warranty, hardware, size and weight are probably the biggest differences between these brands. Here is the warranty breakdown for these seven brands

  • Yeti: 3 year
  • Orca: Lifetime
  • Pelican: Lifetime
  • Bison: 5 year
  • Grizzly: Lifetime
  • K2: 7 year
  • Engel: 3 year

What about "bear proof" coolers?

All of these brands claim their coolers are "bear proof", but that isn't actually true...not without a padlock anyway. Popular Mechanics did an actual bear test and found that a bear could pry open the rubber latches with his teeth, whereas he was unable to open a Pelican cooler with actual press-and-pull latches. I would say it's a benefit to have these types of latches and rubber latches you simply pull to open are a potential weakness, unless you padlock the cooler shut.

So what cooler do you recommend?

If you need a cooler that is actually bear proof without a padlock, get a Pelican. It has a lifetime warranty, a track record of excellent products, and the latches are actually bear proof. If bearproofing isn't really required I would also consider Orca or Grizzly, as they both have lifetime warranties and you can padlock them shut if needed. Orcas and Grizzlys have a form factor more like the Yeti, whereas the Pelican is bulkier.

A few more things to look at when selecting your cooler:

  • Interior dimensions will vary and actual cooler capacity can vary, even if they both specify "65 quart capacity". For instance, Yeti coolers don't tend to hold what they say they do. Outdoor Gear Lab reports the Yeti Tundra 45 actually only holds 38 quarts, whereas the Pelican 45 Elite actually holds 45 quarts. This may or may not matter to you.

  • Some of these coolers are quite a bit heavier than others. Some of this can be attributed to the fact that the cooler is actually bigger (Yeti Tundra 45 vs. Pelican 45 Elite), so it's almost an apples to oranges comparison but even when normalizing for that difference there are some brands who make coolers that are simply bulkier and heavier than others (The Yeti Tundra 45 weighs 25 lbs. whereas the Pelican 45 Elite weighs 35 lbs.). If you're car camping this likely won't be a problem. If you're moving the cooler around a lot, it probably will be.
